newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore asset prices consolidate in 1996 - MAS.
newsitem.headline: Singapore asset prices consolidate in 1996 - MAS.

text.p: Singapore asset prices witnessed some consolidation in 1996, with growth in stock and housing prices moderating through much of the year, the Monetary Authority of Singapore said in its 1996/97 annual report on Tuesday.
It said stock prices remained relatively subdued following the major correction in 1995.
Property prices eased after three years of rapid increase, following the imposition of a package of anti-speculation measures in May 1996.
Private housing prices dipped for the first time since 1990 to close 4.6 percent lower at end 1996 after the curbs.
For the year as a whole, however, prices still managed to record growth of 11 percent, mostly on the initial surge in prices during the first half of 1996.
"Nonetheless, the annual rate of growth in prices was considerably lower than the 30 percent per annum seen during 1993-95," the MAS said.
Public housing flats were relatively unfazed by the May 1996 measures and prices rose 40 percent during the year following average growth of 34 percent in 1993-95.
But the pace of increase is likely to consolidate this year, following the implementation of the Housing Board's curbs on mortgage loans, MAS said.
Price consolidation in office property, which began in 1995, continued through last year with more supply coming on stream.
Office space increased by 519,000 sq m during the period between the fourth quarter of 1995 abd first quarter of 1997, more than double the increase in the previous six quarters.
Industrial property prices also consolidated in 1996 as growth in the manufacturing sector slowed and occupancy rate declined to a seven year low of 94.5 percent in the fourth quarter of last year.
